AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: on_card_played (tuning_fork.py:29-36), dispatched by HookSystem.on_card_played (hooks.py:385-389) from CombatState._resolve_card_play (combat.py:514)
AfterCardPlayed.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Every clause of the relic is faithful -- the Skill test, the >= threshold, the `-= threshold` rather than a zeroing, the 10 and the 7, and (contrary to its own docstring) the per-run counter -- but the sim fires this hook ONCE PER PLAY where C# fires it once per REPLAY ITERATION, so a replayed Skill advances the counter by 1 instead of 2.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): a replayed Skill counts once instead of twice, so the counter drifts and every later trigger in the run is one Skill late
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardModel.cs:1904-1965 builds a fresh CardPlay inside `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` and fires Hook.AfterCardPlayed at line 1961 INSIDE that loop, so TuningFork.AfterCardPlayed (TuningFork.cs:97-109) runs once per iteration. The sim runs the whole play-count loop in CombatState._resolve_card_play and only then calls hooks.on_card_played (combat.py:514). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py axe-tuning`): with the counter preloaded to 9 and a Defend played, the relic alone gives block 12 and counter 0 (correct); with relic/throwing_axe also held -- which makes the first card of each combat play twice, and which is in THIS batch -- the sim gives block 17 and counter 0, where the game gives block 17 and counter **1** (iteration 0: 9 -> 10, GainBlock(7), -= 10 -> 0; iteration 1: 0 -> 1). The block total happens to agree for this one play, but the counter does not, and because the counter is per-run ([SavedProperty], see N1) the offset never washes out: every subsequent Tuning Fork trigger for the rest of the run needs one more Skill in the sim than in the game. Both sides ported: Tuning Fork is Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag, Throwing Axe is granted by the ported Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py:13), and three further ported replay sources reach the same combat.py:469 play-count hook -- the Spiral and Glam enchantments and Hidden Gem's base_replay_count. This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G4 (the per-Replay CardPlay loop) at a third content site, after audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json G1 -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3; the seam owns the machinery and this record owns Tuning Fork's observable. Rule 7: combat.py, hooks.py, events/tanx.py, relics/throwing_axe.py, audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json and audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1 (PROMPT.md bug class 24 -- A DOCSTRING THAT MISDESCRIBES THE PORT AND POINTS AT A FALSE GAP): tuning_fork.py:15-16 says 'the game's counter persists across the run; the sim's is per-combat, like Happy Flower'. The sim's is NOT per-combat, and the code is right
guards.rationale: The CODE keeps `_skills_played` in __init__ (tuning_fork.py:25-27) and never resets it, and sim relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to every CombatState, so the counter is run-scoped. C#'s SkillsPlayed is a [SavedProperty] (TuningFork.cs:59-75) and TuningFork.cs has NO BeforeCombatStart, AfterRoomEntered, AfterCombatEnd or turn-boundary override at all -- so it is run-scoped there too. The two agree; only the comment is wrong. This settles the SECOND LOOK this batch was handed for `_skills_played`, and RE-EXECUTED against the current sweep: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` prints `tuning_fork ['_skills_played'] written by: _skills_played<-['__init__','on_card_played'] C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)`, which is the post-rewrite column (sweep-A defect 3) and is correct. A batch that had trusted the docstring instead of the code would have filed a false gap and 'fixed' a working relic -- exactly what class 24 was written for.

Checked deliberately because audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json G1 is a LIVE gap for exactly the opposite reason -- BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87 DOES skip auto-plays and the sim does not -- and class 29 says never to copy a sibling's verdict across. guards.what: N3: the order of GainBlock and the decrement -- C# grants the block and THEN does `SkillsPlayed -= SkillsThreshold` (TuningFork.cs:105-106); the sim decrements first (tuning_fork.py:34-36)
guards.rationale: Nothing reads SkillsPlayed between the two statements except DisplayAmount (TuningFork.cs:25-35), which is presentation, and CreatureCmd.GainBlock cannot re-enter AfterCardPlayed. So the two orders reach the same state. Recorded because it is exactly the kind of ordering that would matter if the block gain ever triggered another Skill play -- the sim's order is the safer one, and it is not a divergence today.

guards.what: N4: `SkillsPlayed >= SkillsThreshold` and `-=` rather than `== threshold` and `= 0` (TuningFork.cs:102, 106)
guards.rationale: tuning_fork.py:33-34 uses the same `>=` and the same subtraction. This is load-bearing precisely BECAUSE of G1: in the game a replay can push the counter to 11 in one play, and `>=` plus `-= 10` leaves 1 rather than swallowing the overflow. The port would therefore behave correctly if G1 were fixed, without a second change -- worth stating so the fixer does not touch this arithmetic.

guards.what: N5: CardsVar(10) and BlockVar(7m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (TuningFork.cs:39-43) vs SKILLS = 10 and BLOCK = 7 (tuning_fork.py:22-23)
guards.rationale: SkillsThreshold is `DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue` (TuningFork.cs:77) and the block is `DynamicVars.Block` (:105). No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 10 and 7 are the pinned non-ascension values. The Unpowered typing is carried through: tuning_fork.py:36 passes `props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED` to BlockCmd.apply, and `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(base.Owner.Creature, base.DynamicVars.Block, null)` passes cardSource = null, which the sim's call also omits.
